title: Liver anatomy: lobes, vessels and bile ducts
description: The body's chemical plant: metabolism, bile, clotting factors, detoxification and storage.

questions.question: What are the main functions of the liver?
questions.answer: The liver processes nutrients, makes bile and many blood proteins, stores glycogen and participates in drug and toxin metabolism. Its blood arrives from both the portal vein and hepatic artery.

questions.question: Where is the liver located?
questions.answer: Most of the liver lies beneath the diaphragm in the right upper abdomen, with a smaller part extending across the midline.

questions.question: What is the gallbladder?
questions.answer: A 7–10 cm pear-shaped sac on the visceral surface of the right lobe, with fundus, body and neck. Its wall concentrates bile up to tenfold. Function: Stores and concentrates bile, releasing it into the duodenum when fat arrives (CCK-mediated).

questions.question: Where is the hepatic portal vein located?
questions.answer: Formed behind the pancreatic neck by the splenic and superior mesenteric veins; carries nutrient-rich, deoxygenated blood from gut, spleen and pancreas. Function: Delivers 75% of hepatic blood and everything absorbed from the gut for first-pass processing.

questions.question: What is the function of the hepatic lobule & sinusoids?
questions.answer: Function: Blood flows from triad to central vein while bile flows the opposite way, from canaliculi to the triad bile duct. Hexagonal units ~1 mm across: plates of hepatocytes radiating from a central vein, separated by sinusoids lined with endothelium and Kupffer macrophages; portal triads (artery, vein, bile duct) sit at the corners.
